title: Deviation report
purpose: Read the report, its related evidence, investigation and retained review history.
summary: One deviation report: what happened, its linked evidence, investigation and review history.

tasks.title: Complete and submit the report
steps: Select [[Edit]] to fill in the investigation, then [[Submit for review]].

tasks.title: Review it
steps: Managers and administrators: select [[Record review]] to close it or return it for revision.

tasks.title: Reopen a closed report
steps: Managers and administrators: select [[Reopen deviation]] and give a reason.

good_to_know: The reviewer must be someone other than the report's creator and its latest submitter.
A report awaiting review is frozen.
Reports are never deleted, and the history cannot be rewritten.

sections.title: Access and meaning
paragraphs: Administrators, repository managers and technicians record, edit and submit deviations. Viewers read them. Managers and administrators review and reopen them. Inactive accounts and accounts without an application role, including bare superusers, have no access.

These are working product defaults, not repository policy. Deviations retain a report and its investigation, corrective action, effectiveness and independent review. They do not change specimens, stock, storage, linked records or holds. No attachments, deadlines, automatic notifications or risk thresholds are provided.

sections.title: Report and navigation
paragraphs: The header shows the DEV identifier, Open, Awaiting review or Closed status and revision. On this page links jump to Report, Investigation and follow-up, Review facts and History. The breadcrumb returns to Deviations.

items.label: Title
items.description: Required, up to 160 characters. A concise label for finding this report.

items.label: Occurred at
items.description: Required observed timestamp, in repository local time to the second. It must not be in the future. It is distinct from the server-recorded creation and update times.

items.label: Description
items.description: Required report of what was observed, up to 4,000 characters.

items.label: Immediate action
items.description: Optional action already taken, up to 4,000 characters.

items.label: Investigation
items.description: Up to 4,000 characters. Optional while open, required before submission. Explain what is known and explain if unknown.

items.label: Corrective action
items.description: Up to 4,000 characters. Optional while open, required before submission. Explain the action or why none is needed.

items.label: Effectiveness
items.description: Up to 4,000 characters. Optional while open, required before submission. Record evidence or explain why unknown or not applicable.

items.label: Excursion and Inventory audit
items.description: Optional links to existing evidence, in any status. Both can be linked or left blank. Open reports may correct or clear links with a reason; previous link identities remain in history. Linking never changes the related record.

sections.title: Review facts and history
paragraphs: Created shows the original server time and creator; Updated shows the latest saved change. Latest submission shows the latest submitter and time, even after return or reopen. Closed shows the current closure actor and time; a return or reopen has no current closure. Prior decisions remain in history.

History runs oldest to newest with event type, actor, recorded time, reason and complete prior/new values. Blank means no value was recorded. Source links show the current excursion or audit and open that record. Their prior identifiers are retained in history. The record foot identifies this view and who produced it.

items.label: Edit and Submit for review
items.description: Operators can edit or submit an Open report. Submission requires investigation, corrective action and effectiveness; it freezes narratives and source links for review.

items.label: Record review
items.description: Available while Awaiting review to a manager or administrator other than both the original creator and latest submitter. Close records acceptance and freezes the report; Return for revision opens it for further work. Both require a reason. A creator or submitter sees a disabled action and must ask another reviewer.

items.label: Reopen deviation
items.description: Managers and administrators can reopen a Closed report with a reason. Operators can edit and submit again. The previous closure remains in history.

items.label: Read-only
items.description: Viewers see the full report and history without mutation controls. Awaiting review reports are frozen; Closed reports require reopening before edits.

sections.title: Saving and retained history
paragraphs: Every saved change requires a reason and records the actor, server time, revision and full prior and new values. Earlier narratives, source links, submissions and decisions remain in history. Reports cannot be deleted and history cannot be rewritten.

Saving validates and commits the report and its history together or saves nothing. Validation retains entered values. If someone changes the record first, your posted values stay visible and saving is blocked. Cancel, reload the latest record, compare your notes and start again; retrying the old form cannot overwrite the newer report. Do not enter identifying information.
